about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

corn.fundamental: Wet fields have put Iowa's harvest behind, a short-term logistics delay rather than a crop loss. Brazil's strained farm economy (cited by Corteva) does not yet change its record-crop outlook; the RFS waiver requests remain the demand risk.
events: Heavy rains left Iowa fields saturated and harvest behind (AgroLatam).
Corteva flagged Brazil's farm-economy stress in its earnings (Bloomberg).
States' RFS waiver requests threaten ethanol grind (Successful Farming).

soybeans.fundamental: Nothing new on supply; a weaker real today adds to Brazil's export competitiveness against US offers, while US growers are still looking to China for longer-term demand under the tariff overhang.
events: US soybean farmers eye long-term gains in the China market (Brownfield).
A weaker real and ample supply keep Brazilian soybean prices sliding (Czapp, Barchart).
Tariffs continue to limit US sales to China (Brownfield).

meal.fundamental: Meal is riding the soybean complex after the WASDE; no meal-specific supply news since the report.
events: Meal firmed about 1% with soybeans after USDA's stocks cut (Barchart).

oil.fundamental: Policy risk is back: state requests for renewable fuel waivers could trim biomass-based diesel demand if EPA grants them. Palm's El Niño risk still supports the global veg-oil balance, and crude has recovered from its early drop.
events: Biofuel groups warn state RFS waiver requests threaten grain and oilseed demand (Successful Farming, AgWeb).
Petrobras is buying out partners in the Logum pipeline to expand biofuels logistics (Reuters).
Palm oil rose on El Niño risk to Indonesia's 2027 output (Bloomberg).

wheat.fundamental: Wheat gave back its post-WASDE bounce as the spillover support from corn and soybeans faded; cheap French and Argentine origin keeps US export demand under pressure.
events: Wheat fell on Thursday (Barchart).
China booked French and Argentine wheat as global prices slumped (Bloomberg).

kc.fundamental: HRW is following Chicago; Chinese buying of cheap French and Argentine wheat underlines how competitive non-US supply is.
events: KC wheat pushed above first resistance intraday with the broader grain bounce (Barchart).
China's purchases went to French and Argentine origins, not the US (Bloomberg).
Trade deals in progress could lift US cotton and rice exports (Brownfield).
Last week's export sales were the best in seven weeks, led by Vietnam (ADMIS).
cotton.fundamental: A possible demand-side positive: new US trade deals could open more export room for cotton, which matters with commitments still behind the usual pace. Nothing new on old-crop supply or certs today.

hogs.fundamental: Cash hogs stay soft and the cutout near five-year lows keeps pressure on deferred months; front-month gains look like spread adjustment rather than better demand.
events: Lean hogs edged up in front while deferred contracts ended lower (The Pig Site).
Hogs closed mixed Wednesday with weak cash (Barchart).
Pork cutout slipped back toward a five-year low (The Pig Site).

cattle.fundamental: Futures bounced again, but the debate has shifted to demand: imported beef and grid pricing are capping what packers pay, and cheaper beef-on-dairy calves point to more fed supply further out.
events: Cattle futures rebounded even as beef-demand worries grow (AgroLatam).
Beef demand and grid pricing are reshaping the cattle market (Drovers).
Beef-on-dairy calf prices are falling (Dairy Herd).

feeders.fundamental: Weaker fed steer prices and wider feedlot losses cut into what feedlots can pay for replacements, a near-term headwind; the screwworm-driven closure to Mexican feeders still keeps domestic supply tight.
events: Feedlot losses widened as fed steer prices fell (Drovers).
Screwworm spreading faster in milder weather (Bloomberg).
USDA began hiring for its Texas sterile-fly facility (USDA).

class3.fundamental: Block cheese fell at the CME, which hits Class III directly, on top of US milk output at a 30-year high. The Oregon HPAI case is a small local risk at the margin.
events: Cheese blocks and butter led CME dairy declines Thursday (Brownfield).
Oregon reported its first HPAI case in a dairy herd (Feedstuffs).
EPA ended its livestock emissions program (Brownfield).

class4.fundamental: Butter's drop at the CME takes some support out of Class IV; tight nonfat dry milk is still the main prop.
events: Butter led CME dairy declines Thursday (Brownfield).
Tight NDM supplies continue to support Class IV (Czapp, Brownfield).

palm.fundamental: El Niño is now threatening Indonesia's 2027 palm output, a lagged but meaningful supply risk for the largest producer; that outweighs today's softer crude for the veg-oil outlook.
events: Palm oil rose as El Niño threatens Indonesia's 2027 supplies (Bloomberg).
Crude sank on peace optimism, a drag on biodiesel economics (OilPrice.com).

natgas.fundamental: Qatar losing the Polish LNG contract is seen as a real setback to its expansion, reinforcing tighter global LNG supply and the case for US export demand. Near-term US prices still hinge on the coming cold spell.
events: Losing the Orlen LNG deal is a serious blow to Qatar's expansion plans (Bloomberg).
Orlen cancelled its long-term QatarEnergy contract over delivery failures (Reuters, WSJ).
US gas had rallied on a coming cold spell before slipping (WSJ, NGI).

crude.fundamental: The peace trade reversed: Brent briefly reached $94 after Trump said the US had no need for an Iran deal, and WTI is back near 88. Supply is still returning from the Gulf, Saudi Arabia and Nigeria, so the move is a risk-premium reset rather than a new shortage.
events: Brent briefly hit $94 after Trump said the US has no need for an Iran deal (OilPrice.com).
Middle East output is climbing and Nigeria is at its OPEC quota (ADMIS, OilPrice.com).
EIA sees global stocks building this quarter (Dow Jones).

ulsd.fundamental: Diesel bounced with crude as Iran-deal optimism faded; the domestic distillate squeeze persists because Russian diesel is not reaching the US.
events: Crude rebounded after Trump said a deal with Iran is not needed (OilPrice.com).
Russian diesel exports doubled, none to the US (Financial Times).
The US plan to import Russian diesel has stalled (WSJ).

rbob.fundamental: Gasoline recovered with crude once the Iran peace optimism faded; California refinery closures remain a regional rather than national tightening theme.
events: Crude rebounded after Trump said a deal with Iran is not needed (OilPrice.com).
California refinery closures are reshaping West Coast flows (OilPrice.com).
